context: Wilde to Frank Harris, 2 September 1900, Paris. Six weeks before the quarrel over the same play. Here the tone is still easy — he sets out the Bellew and Mrs Potter agreements plainly, complains that Harris never writes, and ends on Mellor and melancholia.
quote:
Hotel d’Alsace, Rue des Beaux Arts, Paris. Sept. 2.

My dear Frank, Since you left Paris I have not received, till this morning, a single line from you on any subject. It is curious that your letter should have gone astray, as the post is usually all right.

I don’t know that it was quite wise of you to speak to Mrs Potter — she holds the agreement for the play. I cannot, as I told you, break with her — it is impossible.

I thought, from not hearing from you, that you had given up the idea of writing the scene — (the third act scene).

I first received from Kyrle Bellew £5 a week — but after five weeks he ceased payment, and the agreement lapsed in consequence.

I then got £100 from Mrs Potter and a new agreement was signed.

On the completion of the play I am to receive more down — and of course, on its production, royalties.

It is a great bore that you never write — now that you have a type-writer you might let me hear from you.

I am in my usual state — drifting along: I wish I had your concentration of purpose, and controlled intellect. My last visit to Mellor has given me melancholia — I must go no more. Ever Oscar
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 46-47. One sheet of Grand Cafe, 14 Boulevard des Capucines paper folded once, four sides: image 46 is the recto (sides 1 and 2, left to right), image 47 the verso (sides 3 and 4); the letterhead shows through mirrored at the top of 47, which is what confirms the order. Wilde writes 'Hotel d'Alsace' over the printed heading without striking it out, unlike the Ives letters on the same stock. Emphasis: none on any of the four sides, a null finding, and the volume prints no italic either — the two agree. Read with care: 'till this morning' looks underlined at page size and is not; the stroke is the long crossbar of his t, continuous with the letter, confirmed at 4.2x. Dateline: 'Sept. 2.' is not underlined here, where '_Friday_', '_Thursday_' and '_Saturday_' all were. So the underlined dateline is his habit, not his rule. Punctuation: his dashes restored throughout; the volume gives full stops. 1173 - stand, because there the edition read a real difference.
